sections.title: Stage 5 · Ace: speed and flash
sections.html:
Stage 5 · Ace: speed and flash

Nine lessons that move the skill from the hand to the head. Fast hands on the beads, five lines in the head, the first flash rounds, and the first Bead Score.

Where this stage goes

The level goal. Ten 3-digit lines on the soroban in under a minute, five 2-digit numbers in the head, and your first flash anzan.

In plain words. Fast hands on the beads, five two-digit numbers added in the head, a first flash round and a first Bead Score. This is when other people start to notice.

How long. 6–8 weeks at fifteen minutes a day, six days a week.

Speed is not a bonus. It is what moves the skill from the hand to the mind. When the fingers run on their own, attention is free to hold the picture.

Three things happen in this stage. The hands get fast on the real soroban, on columns of ten 3-digit lines. The mental abacus grows to two rods and five lines. And your child meets flash anzan: numbers shown one at a time, gone before they can be said, with the total kept on the mental beads.

The stage ends with the first Bead Score. Write it down. Your child will beat it.

The drills in this stage

  • Written, timed. Ten-line columns of 3-digit numbers, then 4-digit columns. Time the sheet.
  • Flash. You show number cards one at a time at a set beat, or say them at that beat. One-digit numbers at 1.5 seconds, then at 1 second.
  • Listening. You read numbers aloud and your child adds them on the mental beads. This is how abacus schools run dictation.
  • Mental. Five 2-digit lines in the head, adds first, then plus and minus.
  • Bead Score. The ladder test in the trainer: no soroban, no paper, no help.

Accuracy before speed

This is the stage with the most clocks, and it is where accuracy matters most. Speed up only when the last three sheets were 8 of 10 or better. A child who is right half the time at a fast beat is guessing. A child who is right nine times out of ten at a slow beat is building the picture, and the beat will follow.

Where this sits on the abacus ladders

Mapped to UCMAS, Ace opens Construction, the middle module. Five 2-digit lines in the head is the format of the 4th kyu mental exam in Japan. The flash rounds here start at Bead Score rung 7, five one-digit numbers at one second, which is about 18th kyu on the Japanese flash anzan ladder.

Parent lineWrite the day's time on the fridge. Kids love watching a number fall.

sections.title: Lesson 5.1 · Fast hands
sections.html:
Lesson 5.1 · Fast hands

Lesson 34 of 76. Stage 5, lesson 1 of 9. About 12 minutes. You need your soroban and a grown-up beside you.

By the end, your child can add ten 3-digit lines on the soroban with a quick, quiet hand.

The move

Speed comes from the hand, not from hurry. Thumb and index finger only. Fingers stay close to the beads and never lift high.

The eyes read the next number while the hand finishes the last. Do not look back at the beads to check. Trust the hand.

Ten lines of three digits, adding only. Target: all right first. Then under 90 seconds a column. Then under 60.

Parent lineWatch the hand, not the clock, and say something when the fingers stay low and quiet.

Lesson 5.2 · Read ahead

Lesson 35 of 76. Stage 5, lesson 2 of 9. About 12 minutes. You need your soroban and a grown-up beside you.

By the end, your child can work ten-line 3-digit columns with plus and minus mixed, reading each sign and number as one chunk.

The move

Mixed plus and minus, ten lines. The sign is part of the number. Read "minus 347" as one chunk, not a sign and then a number.

The hand needs to know which way to move before it gets there. Reading the whole line at once is what keeps it moving.

Lesson 5.3 · Four digits

Lesson 36 of 76. Stage 5, lesson 3 of 9. About 12 minutes. You need your soroban and a grown-up beside you.

By the end, your child can work 5-line columns of 4-digit numbers, thousands first.

The move

Four rods. Thousands first. The soroban does not care how long a number is. Only the eyes do.

Use the dots on the beam to find the thousands rod fast. Most sorobans mark every third rod.

sections.title: Lesson 5.4 · Flash anzan begins
sections.html:
Lesson 5.4 · Flash anzan begins

Lesson 37 of 76. Stage 5, lesson 4 of 9. About 8 minutes. You need a grown-up to show or read the numbers. No soroban, no paper.

By the end, your child can add five one-digit numbers shown one at a time, keeping the total on the mental beads.

The move

A number appears for a moment and goes. Add it to the mental beads. The next one appears. At the end, say the total.

Nothing can be written and nothing can be looked at again. The picture does all the work.

Start easy. Five one-digit numbers, each shown for one and a half seconds. The feeling you want is calm. The number lands on the beads and is gone.

Champions go a long way past this. The world record, set in 2024, is fifteen 3-digit numbers in 1.61 seconds. Your child is on the same ladder, on the first rung.

Worked example. Five numbers, one at a time.

  • Number 1: 3. Mental beads: .
  • Number 2: 5. Mental beads: .
  • Number 3: 1. Mental beads: .
  • Number 4: 4. Mental beads: .
  • Number 5: 2. Mental beads: .
  • Say 15.
Parent lineMake the cards with a thick pen, hold a steady beat, and show each one once.

Lesson 5.5 · Flash: faster, longer

Lesson 38 of 76. Stage 5, lesson 5 of 9. About 8 minutes. You need a grown-up to show or read the numbers. No soroban, no paper.

By the end, your child can add eight one-digit numbers flashed at one second each.

The move

Eight numbers at one second each.

If the picture goes, do not chase it. Let the next number land anyway. Your child will often still be right.

sections.title: Lesson 5.6 · Mental: five 2-digit numbers

Lesson 5.6 · Mental: five 2-digit numbers

Lesson 39 of 76. Stage 5, lesson 6 of 9. About 10 minutes. You need no soroban. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can add five 2-digit numbers in the head.

The move

Five lines of two digits, in the head.

Move the fingers on the table if it helps. Most children do at this point and stop on their own later.

Worked example. Picture 47. Add 36, then 25.

  • + 36. Tens rod, plus 3: add 5, take away 2. Ones rod, plus 6: take away 5, add 1, carry 1. Tens rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now .

Lesson 5.7 · Mental: 2-digit plus and minus

Lesson 40 of 76. Stage 5, lesson 7 of 9. About 10 minutes. You need no soroban. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can add and take away five 2-digit numbers in the head.

The move

Same as last time, with take-aways in the mix.

Borrows in the head feel strange the first week and normal the second. If a borrow will not come, go back to the beads for one sum, then close the eyes and replay it.

Worked example. Five lines, plus and minus.

sections.title: Lesson 5.8 · Listening: numbers read aloud

Lesson 5.8 · Listening: numbers read aloud

Lesson 41 of 76. Stage 5, lesson 8 of 9. About 8 minutes. You need a grown-up to read the numbers aloud. No soroban.

By the end, your child can add four 2-digit numbers read aloud, on the mental beads, at about one number a second.

The move

You read numbers out loud and your child adds them on the mental beads. This is how abacus schools run their mental drills: the teacher calls, the class answers.

It also means anyone can practise with your child. A grandparent or a babysitter only needs to read a list at a steady beat. Nobody needs to know any math.

Say each number once, clearly. Say "minus" as part of the number.

Worked example. Three numbers, read aloud.

  • Number 1: 34. Mental beads: .
  • Number 2: 28. Mental beads: .
  • Number 3: 17. Mental beads: .
  • Say 79.

sections.title: Lesson 5.9 · Your first Bead Score
sections.html:
Lesson 5.9 · Your first Bead Score

Lesson 42 of 76. Stage 5, lesson 9 of 9. About 10 minutes. You need no soroban. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can take the Bead Score ladder for the first time and write down the number.

The move

The Bead Score is a ladder. Easy rungs first, harder each step, until one fails. The score is the top rung cleared. No soroban, no paper, no help.

It lives in the trainer, because the flash rungs need exact timing. This page is the warm-up: ten head sums to wake the picture up.

Then take the test. Write the number on the fridge in your child's own hand. Retake it every two to four weeks, never on a tired day.

Parent lineThe first Bead Score is the one your child will beat, so make a fuss of writing it down.

Drill

sections.title: The Ace Boss
sections.html:
The Ace Boss

Take the boss after the first Bead Score, once the flash pages pass at one second. Part 1 maps to Lessons 5.1 and 5.2. Part 2 maps to 5.7. Part 3 maps to 5.5.

The printed test is Boss 5 in boss-tests.md. It has 3 parts:

  • 3-digit, 10 lines. 4 problems on your soroban, 5 minutes total. Need 3 of 4 in 5 minutes.
  • Mental 2-digit. 5 problems, five lines each. Need 4 of 5 in 4 minutes.
  • Flash. 5 rounds, eight 1-digit numbers at 1 second. Need 4 of 5 in 3 minutes.

sections.title: What the trainer adds to this stage
sections.html:
What the trainer adds to this stage

Flash is the one drill that is hard to run well by hand. A parent with cards can hold a one-second beat. Nobody can hold 0.7 seconds for long, and later stages go to a fifth of a second.

The trainer flashes numbers on screen at the exact speed, reads numbers aloud for listening drills, and runs the Bead Score ladder. The score goes on an age chart, with your child's own line climbing test by test.

Everything else in this stage works on paper. The flash pages here are built so you can run them at the table, and the trainer is there for the speeds your hands cannot keep.
